{{Quote|[Xesh] was taken to his masters' machines&mdash;encased in a tomblike shell where he screamed in fear. Around him, he sensed his brood mates, shrieking in the darkness. He learned anger and hate. Later, he understood that this bleak anger&mdash;this dark hatred&mdash;was the Force and the power that fed his masters' ships.|Force Hound Xesh was discovered to be Force-sensitive during his time as Force-drive fuel|<ref name="DotJ:TPoB1">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 1]]</ref>}}
The '''Force-drive''',<ref name="TUR" /> also known as '''Force-based hyperdrive'''<ref name="TEA" /> or '''Rakatan hyperdrive''',<ref name="TNEC" /> was a type of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Engine/Legends|drive]] used in the [[skipship]]s of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].<ref name="TUR" /> As its name suggested, the Force-drive was powered by the [[The Force/Legends|Force energies]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and was only capable of transit to worlds with strong [[Vergence/Legends|Force signatures]].<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>

==Description==
{{Quote|The Rakatan hyperdrive was of no use for traveling between arbitrary points in realspace, General. It didn't work that way. Rather, it honed ''[sic]'' in on the signature of worlds strong in the Force — ones brimming with life, in other words.|Dr. Insmot Bowen explains the Force-drive to General Arhul Kurumenga|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:XeshForceDrive-ForceStorm5.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tasha Ryo's vision of Xesh in the Force-drive]]
The Force-drive was a type of [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] that powered [[Warship/Legends|warships]] using the wells of [[The Force/Legends|Force]] energy existing within sentient [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] [[Species/Legends|species]] as fuel.<ref name="EGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Force-drives were installed aboard the [[Rakatan ship]]s, where entire rooms were dedicated to the storage of slave fuel in vast containment racks. Each rack contained a number of "tomblike shells," cells wherein the slaves were restrained face-down and hooked to a set of electrodes. Turned into living batteries, they were subjected to intense pain for extended periods of time, with the resultant [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side energy]] extracted and channeled to the Force-drive.<ref name="DotJ:TPoB1" />

While this system did work, the Force-drive's reliance on the Force as its primarily power source gave it certain limitations, the most important of which was its inability to travel between any two arbitrary points in [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]]. The Force-drive was only capable of targeting worlds with strong [[Vergence/Legends|Force signatures]], a fact which resulted in an empire that spanned the breadth of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> but which only incorporated more than five hundred worlds.<ref name="GH05">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 05: Rise of the Infinite Empire}}</ref> In addition, a powerful prisoner with a strong will could overcome the destructive effects of the mechanisms and break out of their cell.<ref name="DotJ:FW4">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force War 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force War'' 4]]</ref>

==History==
===Infinite Empire===
{{Quote|Long ago, we Rakata were a great space-faring people. Our ships combined technology and the power of the Force, and we were able to pilot them to the farthest reaches of the galaxy.|Orsaa|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
Many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before [[36,453 BBY]], the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] uplifted the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] civilization of [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], who were taught the power of the Force and were given advanced technology. Following the devastating [[Battle between the Kwa and the Rakata|conflict with the Kwa]], the Rakata promptly developed<ref name="DotJ:TPoB4" /> the first known hyperdrive,<ref name="GH05" /> discovering that they could use the energy of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] slaves among the populations they conquered to fuel their warships. Thus the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] was born, which expanded with each new conquest and discovery of another planet rich in the Force.<ref name="DotJ:TPoB4" />

When a plague stripped the Rakata of their Force-sensitivity, they lost their ability to wield their Force-based technology. The Infinite Empire collapsed and the remaining survivors fled to an isolated region in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] known as the [[Rakatan Archipelago]]. While most of tribes in the Archipelago reverted to primitivism, some tribes recovered the technology of their ancestors. Buried [[skipship]]s exhumed on [[Makatak]] and [[Tulpaa]] turned the Rakata into spacefarers once more. The Rakata's Force-blindness meant they could only operate the ship's machinery at a fraction of its functionality. The ship's Force-drives zeroed in on life-rich planets across the Rakatan Archipelago, but the Rakata had no control over this process. The [[Makatak tribe|Makatak]] and [[Tulpaa tribe|Tulpaa Rakata's]] Force-drives brought them to the same unspoiled planets, leading to resource wars between them.<ref name="TUR" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|You said we took their technology. But hyperdrives and blasters don't require the Force.''"<br />"''Correct, General — in fact, the Rakata were careful to keep Force-sensitive slaves away from their machines. But that drove their slaves to take their technology and reverse-engineer it, eliminating the role of focusing crystals and anything else that required the Force. Duros, Herglics, Baragwin, Devaronians, Gossam and of course the Coruscanti all experimented with hyperspace cannons, tumbledrives, pulse cannons and other derivatives of Rakatan technologies.|General Arhul Kurumenga and Dr. Insmot Bowen discuss the legacy of the Force-drive|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
Although the Rakata did not reveal the secret of their technologies to the slaves, over time, they did discover the secret of the hyperdrive and many other technologies.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The [[Gossam/Legends|Gossams]] and [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]] created a [[Tumbledrive/Legends|tumble hyperdrive]] even before the fall of the Infinite Empire, while [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] traveled without a hyperdrive at all, sending colonial [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]] across the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. In turn, [[Corellian/Legends|Corellians]] and [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] independently reverse-engineered [[hyperspace cannon]]s from the Rakatan hyperdrive, but it was the development of the modern hyperdrive by Corellian scientists around [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]] that opened up the galaxy to interstellar trade and led to the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The latter, representing an amalgamation of various emerging civilizations, also combined developments based on Rakata technologies.<ref name="TEA" />

Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]], a specialist in [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] history at the [[Obroan Institute for Archaeology]], gave a debriefing in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] to [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arhul Kurumenga]] of the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], and [[Master of Imperial Projects]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]] relating to the history of the Rakata and their technologies, including the Rakatan hyperdrive.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
